name: @kitora/keyboard
description: Kitora's keyboard kit: a framework-free command registry, keybinding layers with user overrides, when-clauses, chords and sequences, conflict analysis, DOM dispatch, roving focus, React bindings, a VS Code-style shortcuts editor, a cheatsheet, palette rows and key hints.

exports.name: isMember
exports.description: True when `value` is one of `set`'s members; narrows an unchecked string (JSON, user input).
exports.signature: <const T extends readonly string[]>(set: T, value: unknown) => value is T[number]

exports.name: MODIFIERS
exports.description:
Modifier names a binding may use. `Mod` is the platform's primary modifier:
Cmd (`Meta`) on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere (K4); it is resolved at match time, so
one keymap serves every platform.

exports.name: Modifier
exports.description: One of `MODIFIERS`: a modifier name a binding may use.

exports.name: PLATFORMS
exports.description: Platforms a binding can vary by (K42) and `Mod` resolves against (K4).

exports.name: Platform
exports.description: One of `PLATFORMS`: `mac`, `win` or `linux`.

exports.name: MATCH_BY
exports.description:
How a chord's key is compared. `key` = the logical `KeyboardEvent.key`, so a
shortcut follows the letter on the keycap (Cmd+Z stays on Z for AZERTY users);
`code` = the physical `KeyboardEvent.code`, written `[KeyW]`, for
position-based keys such as WASD (K2).

exports.name: MatchBy
exports.description: One of `MATCH_BY`: whether a chord matches the logical key or the physical code.

exports.name: KEYMAP_LAYERS
exports.description:
Where a keybinding rule comes from (K37). Later layers win: a user rule beats
a plugin rule beats a default rule, and a `-command` rule removes bindings from
the layers below it (K38).

exports.name: KeymapLayer
exports.description: One of `KEYMAP_LAYERS`: the layer a rule lives in; later layers win.

exports.name: KEY_EVENT_TYPES
exports.description: Which key event a binding listens to (K11). Sequences are keydown only.

exports.name: KeyEventType
exports.description: One of `KEY_EVENT_TYPES`: `keydown` or `keyup`.

exports.name: REPEAT_POLICIES
exports.description: Whether an auto-repeated keydown (a held key) runs the command again (K10).

exports.name: RepeatPolicy
exports.description: One of `REPEAT_POLICIES`: whether a held key runs the command again.

exports.name: INPUT_POLICIES
exports.description:
Whether a binding fires while focus is in an editable field (K88, K89).
`smart` (the default) lets combos with Ctrl, Meta or Alt and the Escape key
through and blocks plain typing keys; `allow` always fires; `ignore` never
fires in a field.

exports.name: InputPolicy
exports.description: One of `INPUT_POLICIES`: whether a binding fires while focus is in an editable field.

exports.name: INVOKED_BY
exports.description: How a command was run, handed to every middleware (K123).

exports.name: InvokedBy
exports.description: One of `INVOKED_BY`: how a command was run.

exports.name: RUN_STATUSES
RunStatus
exports.description: One of `RUN_STATUSES`: the outcome of `run`.

exports.name: DISPATCH_OUTCOMES
exports.description:
What one key event did. `ran` = a command was started; `pending` = the key
was the start of a longer sequence and the engine is waiting (K22); `no-match`
= no binding wants it; `ignored` = the engine refused to look (composition,
paused, a modifier alone, …), with the reason in the decision.

exports.name: DispatchOutcome
exports.description: One of `DISPATCH_OUTCOMES`: what one key event did.

exports.name: IGNORE_REASONS
exports.description:
Why a key event was ignored before any binding was compared (part of the K35
trace). `owned` is decided by the dom layer: a focused widget declared the key
its own (K92), so the engine was never asked.

exports.name: IgnoreReason
exports.description: One of `IGNORE_REASONS`: why a key event was ignored before any binding was compared.

exports.name: RULE_VERDICTS
exports.description:
Why one rule did not fire for a key (the K35 explain trace).
- `chord`: the key or modifiers differ
- `event-type`: a keyup rule on a keydown, or the reverse
- `when`: its `when` clause is false here
- `disabled-rule`: the binding was switched off (K32)
- `disabled-command`: the command's enablement is false (K49)
- `unknown-command`: no command with that id is registered
- `input`: focus is in a field and the rule's input policy blocks it (K89)
- `overlay`: an overlay is on top and the rule belongs to the page or another overlay (K28)
- `character-key`: single-character shortcuts are switched off and the rule starts with one (K129, WCAG 2.1.4)
- `shadowed`: a higher-priority rule took the key
- `removed`: a `-command` rule removed it (K38)
- `fired`: this rule ran

exports.name: RuleVerdict
exports.description: One of `RULE_VERDICTS`: why one rule did or did not fire for a key.

exports.name: FINDING_KINDS
exports.description:
What the keymap analysis reports (K34, K36, K24, K144).
- `conflict`: two rules in the same layer bind the same keys under `when`s that can both be true
- `shadowed`: a higher layer binds the same keys as a lower one (expected for user overrides)
- `prefix`: one binding is the start of another, so the shorter waits for the timeout
- `reserved`: the browser or OS keeps the key (Cmd+W, Ctrl+T, …), so the page never sees it
- `invalid`: the key string or `when` clause does not parse, or the command is unknown
- `screen-reader`: the binding starts with a key screen readers take in browse mode (K132); reported when analysis is asked for it

exports.name: FindingKind
exports.description: One of `FINDING_KINDS`: what a keymap analysis finding reports.

exports.name: CONFLICT_POLICIES
exports.description: What registration does with a `conflict` or `invalid` finding (K34).

exports.name: ConflictPolicy
exports.description: One of `CONFLICT_POLICIES`: what registration does with a conflict or invalid rule.

exports.name: CHANGE_KINDS
exports.description: What a subscriber is told changed (K124). `settings` = the single-character switch (K129).

exports.name: ChangeKind
exports.description: One of `CHANGE_KINDS`: what a subscriber is told changed.

exports.name: ANY_OVERLAY
exports.description: A rule's `overlay` value that takes part whatever is on top (K28): a help key, a global palette key.

exports.name: DEFAULT_SEQUENCE_TIMEOUT_MS
exports.description: How long a started sequence waits for its next key (K23), the common default (tinykeys, Mousetrap).

exports.name: isCharacter
exports.description: True for one printable character (`"a"`, `"?"`, `"é"`, `"@"`), as opposed to a named key.

exports.name: isLetter
exports.description: True for an ASCII letter. Letters are compared case-insensitively; Shift is then explicit.

exports.name: isDigit
exports.description: True for an ASCII digit `0`–`9`.

exports.name: isSymbol
exports.description:
True for a printable ASCII symbol (`?`, `/`, `!`, `@`, …): neither a letter nor
a digit. A symbol already says whether Shift was needed on the user's layout,
so Shift is not compared for symbols unless the binding names it (K8).

exports.name: isNonAsciiCharacter
exports.description: True for a single character outside printable ASCII: a non-Latin layout (`с`) or a macOS Option symbol (`œ`).

exports.name: normalizeKeyName
exports.description:
The canonical name of a key token from a binding string, or `null` when it
names no key (K144 reports it). Single characters are lower-cased (letters are
matched case-insensitively), named keys take their `KeyboardEvent.key`
spelling whatever case was written, and aliases (`esc`, `plus`, …) resolve.

exports.name: isCodeName
exports.description: True when `code` is shaped like a `KeyboardEvent.code` (`KeyW`, `Digit1`, `Numpad1`, `F5`).

exports.name: strokeKey
exports.description: The stroke's key in the canonical spelling `normalizeKeyName` gives a binding token (`" "` → `Space`, `"K"` → `k`).

exports.name: isComposingStroke
exports.description: An IME owns the key: never a shortcut, never part of a sequence (K9).

exports.name: isModifierStroke
exports.description: The modifier key itself (Shift, Control, …), pressed or released alone.

exports.name: usKeyForCode
exports.description:
The key a US QWERTY layout puts at `code`, in canonical spelling, or
`undefined` for codes with no fixed meaning. Used as the fallback when a
layout produced a non-Latin or Option-layer character (K3) and for digit-row
bindings on layouts whose digit row types symbols (AZERTY).

exports.name: stroke
exports.description:
Builds a `KeyStroke` with every modifier up unless given. For tests, scripted
presses and the recorder; the dom layer builds strokes from real events.

exports.name: KeyStroke
exports.description:
One key event as data. A DOM `KeyboardEvent` carries every field except
`altGraph`, which the dom layer reads with `getModifierState("AltGraph")`
(K7). `keyCode` is read for one thing only: 229 marks an IME event in
browsers that do not set `isComposing` on the first one (K9).

exports.name: IME_KEY_CODE
exports.description: `keyCode` an IME reports while it owns the key (`isComposing` can still be false on the first event).

exports.name: DEAD_KEY
exports.description: The `key` of a dead key (accent waiting for the next letter, K14).

exports.name: MODIFIER_KEYS
exports.description: `key` values of the modifier keys themselves: pressing one alone is never a shortcut press.

exports.name: NAMED_KEYS
exports.description:
Named (multi-character) keys a binding may use, in `KeyboardEvent.key`
spelling, which is also the canonical spelling. `Space` stands for `" "`
because a binding string is split on spaces. Function keys `F1`–`F24` are
accepted by pattern (`FUNCTION_KEY`).

exports.name: NamedKey
exports.description: One of `NAMED_KEYS`: a non-character key name a binding may use (`Enter`, `ArrowUp`, `PageDown`, …).

exports.name: KEY_ALIASES
exports.description:
Lower-cased spellings people write for named and symbol keys, mapped to the
canonical name. Symbol names exist so a binding can name `+` and space-like
keys without breaking the `+` / space grammar (`Mod+Plus`).

exports.name: KeyAlias
exports.description: A lower-cased alias spelling (`esc`, `plus`, …); the type-level grammar accepts exactly these (K141).

exports.name: StrokeInit
exports.description: Which modifier flags a stroke carries, as an object; the default for every flag is `false`.

exports.name: modifierFromToken
exports.description: The modifier a token names, or `undefined`.

exports.name: parseChord
exports.description: Parses one chord (`Mod+Shift+P`, `[Shift]+?`, `[KeyW]`). Throws `BindingParseError` with the whole binding as `input`.

exports.name: parseBinding
exports.description: Parses a binding string into its chords (K20–K22). Throws `BindingParseError` (K144).

exports.name: tryParseBinding
exports.description: `parseBinding` that returns the error instead of throwing, for validation passes.
exports.signature: (text: string) => { readonly binding: Binding; } | { readonly error: BindingParseError; }

exports.name: resolveModifiers
exports.description: Replaces the symbolic `Mod` bit with Meta (macOS) or Ctrl (K4).

exports.name: resolveChord
exports.description: A chord with `Mod` resolved for `platform`: what the user's keyboard actually needs.

exports.name: formatChord
exports.description:
The canonical string of a chord: modifiers in a fixed order, optional ones in
brackets, letters upper-cased (`Mod+Shift+P`, `[Shift]+?`, `[KeyW]`). Parsing
it gives the same chord back, so it is the comparison key for conflicts and
the stored form for recorded keys (K19).

exports.name: formatBinding
exports.description: The canonical string of a binding: its chords' canonical strings joined by spaces.

exports.name: normalizeBinding
exports.description: Re-spells a binding string canonically (`ctrl+shift+p` → `Ctrl+Shift+P`). Throws on a bad string.

exports.name: binding
exports.description:
A binding string checked at compile time (K141) and at run time (K144):
`binding("Mod+Shift+P")` returns its argument; `binding("Mod+Kx")` does not
compile, and a string that slips through (a widened `string`) throws here.
exports.signature: <const S extends string>(text: S & ValidBinding<S>) => S

exports.name: MOD_BITS
exports.description: Modifier bits. `MOD` is symbolic until `resolveModifiers` turns it into `META` (macOS) or `CTRL`.

exports.name: MODIFIER_ALIASES
exports.description: Every spelling a modifier token may take, lower-cased.

exports.name: Chord
exports.description: One press of a binding.

exports.name: Binding
exports.description: A parsed binding: its chords in the order they are pressed (one for a combo, more for a sequence).

exports.name: BindingParseError
exports.description: A binding string that does not parse. `input` is the whole string; `reason` says what is wrong (K144).

exports.name: ValidBinding
exports.description: `S` when it is a valid binding string, otherwise `never` (K141).

exports.name: strokeModifiers
exports.description: The modifier bits a stroke carries (`MOD_BITS`, never `Mod`).

exports.name: isShortcutCandidate
exports.description: True when the stroke can be a shortcut press at all (not composing, not a lone dead key, not a modifier alone).

exports.name: matchChord
exports.description: True when `stroke` is the press `chord` describes on `platform`.
exports.signature: (chord: Chord, stroke: KeyStroke, platform: Platform) => boolean

exports.name: strokeToChordString
exports.description:
The canonical string of the chord a stroke presses (K19): `Mod` for the
platform's primary modifier, letters upper-cased (`Mod+Shift+P`, `?`,
`Alt+ArrowUp`). `null` for a stroke that can never be a shortcut press (a
modifier alone, composition). The recorder and devtools store this form;
parsing it gives a chord that matches the same stroke.

exports.name: parseWhen
exports.description: Parses a `when` string into its tree. Throws `WhenParseError`.

exports.name: isTruthy
exports.description: Truthiness of a context value: non-empty string, non-zero number, `true`, non-empty list.

exports.name: evaluateNode
exports.description: Evaluates a parsed tree against context keys.

exports.name: compileWhen
exports.description: The parsed tree of a `when` string, cached. Throws `WhenParseError`.

exports.name: evaluateWhen
exports.description: True when `when` holds for `ctx`; an absent clause always holds.

exports.name: whenAll
exports.description: Several clauses that must all hold (`undefined` entries are skipped).

exports.name: whensMayOverlap
exports.description:
False only when the two clauses provably cannot hold together (`listFocus`
vs `!listFocus`, `view == 'grid'` vs `view == 'list'`). Anything it cannot
reason about (functions, `||`, regexes) counts as overlapping, so the
conflict detector errs towards reporting.
exports.signature: (a: When | undefined, b: When | undefined) => boolean

exports.name: whenKeys
exports.description: The context keys a `when` clause reads, in first-seen order; `[]` for a function clause or one that does not parse (devtools list them next to their values).

exports.name: WhenFn
exports.description: A predicate over context keys.

exports.name: When
exports.description: A `when` clause: a predicate, or a string in the grammar above.

exports.name: WhenNode
exports.description: The parsed form of a `when` string.

exports.name: WhenParseError
exports.description: A `when` string that does not parse; `position` is the character offset of the problem.

exports.name: createContextKeys
exports.description: Creates an empty context key store.

exports.name: ContextValue
exports.description: A value a context key can hold. Lists serve the `in` operator.

exports.name: ContextReader
exports.description: Read access to context keys, all a `when` clause needs.

exports.name: ContextProvider
exports.description:
Computes keys on read (K121). `keys` lists exact names; `prefix` claims every
key starting with it (`route.` → `route.path`, `route.params.id`). A value set
with `set` wins over a provider for the same key.

exports.name: ContextKeys
exports.description: The context key store.

exports.name: messageText
exports.description: The text of a `Message` now.

exports.name: defineCommands
exports.description:
Declares commands as data with their arg types inferred per id (K58, K142):
`defineCommands({ "nav.goto": { title: "Go to", run: (args: { route: string }) => … } })`.
The returned object is the input, typed for `createKeyboard<typeof manifest>()`.

exports.name: createCommandRegistry
exports.description: Creates an empty registry.

exports.name: Message
exports.description: Text that may be translated at read time (K59): a string, or a function returning the current locale's string.

exports.name: RunContext
exports.description: What a command's `run` receives besides its args.

exports.name: CommandSpec
exports.description:
A command. `A` is its argument type (`undefined` = takes none, K48). `when`
decides visibility (palette, cheatsheet, menus) and `enabled` decides whether
it can run (K49); a hidden command can still be enabled for code that runs it
by id, and a visible one can be disabled with a `disabledReason` shown greyed.

exports.name: CommandManifest
exports.description:
A static manifest: command id → spec (K58). Ids are namespaced
(`datagrid.selectAll`, K125). `run` is declared with method syntax, which
TypeScript checks bivariantly, so a spec whose `run` takes `{ route: string }`
fits `CommandSpec<unknown>` here while `ArgsOf` still reads the precise type
from the manifest's own literal type.

exports.name: CommandId
exports.description: The ids of a manifest (K140).

exports.name: ArgsOf
exports.description:
The argument type of command `C`, read from its `run` (K142): `undefined` for
a `run` with no parameter. In an untyped registry (`CommandManifest` itself)
every command takes `unknown`.

exports.name: RunArgs
exports.description: The rest parameters of `run(id, …)`: none, optional or required, from the command's args.

exports.name: RunResult
exports.description: The result of running a command (K50).

exports.name: Invocation
exports.description: One run on its way through the middleware chain (K120, K123).

exports.name: Middleware
exports.description:
Wraps every run (K57, K120): log, time, veto (return `{ status: "vetoed" }`
without calling `next`), report errors, record analytics by `invokedBy`
(K123). `name` identifies a veto's author in the result.

exports.name: CommandEntry
exports.description: A registered command and who registered it (a plugin name, or `undefined` for the host).

exports.name: CommandRegistry
exports.description: The registry inside a keyboard engine.

exports.name: keyTextFor
exports.description: The text of a rule on a platform (variant, else `key`).

exports.name: createKeymap
exports.description: Creates an empty keymap resolved for `platform`.

exports.name: KeybindingRule
exports.description: One keybinding rule (VS Code's keybindings.json shape plus the kit's policies).

exports.name: CompiledRule
exports.description: A rule as the engine sees it after compilation.

exports.name: InvalidRule
exports.description: A rule that failed to compile (K144).

exports.name: KeymapHandle
exports.description: Returned by `add`: switches the rules off and on (K32) or removes them.

exports.name: AddOptions
exports.description: Options for `Keymap.add`.

exports.name: Keymap
exports.description: Rules and their resolution for one platform.

exports.name: ImportReport
exports.description: What `Keymap.importUser` did: how many rules it kept and why the others were rejected.

exports.name: isCharacterChord
exports.description: True when `chord` is a printable character key with no command modifier (Shift allowed).

exports.name: isCharacterBinding
exports.description: True when the binding's first press is a character key alone: what the WCAG 2.1.4 switch turns off (K129).

exports.name: isScreenReaderKey
exports.description:
Keys screen readers take for browse-mode / quick-navigation in a web page
(K132): NVDA browse mode and JAWS virtual cursor use nearly every letter
(h headings, k links, b buttons, e edits, f form fields, t tables, l lists,
i list items, g graphics, d landmarks, …, Shift for the reverse direction)
and the digits 1–6 for heading levels; VoiceOver's single-key Quick Nav uses
the same letters. So every ASCII letter and digit is listed: in browse mode
the reader consumes the key and the page never sees it, and in focus or
application mode the shortcut hijacks the reader's navigation key.

exports.name: startsWithScreenReaderKey
exports.description: True when the binding starts with a screen-reader browse-mode key (K132).

exports.name: withModifier
exports.description:
The binding text with `modifier` added to its first chord (K130): `g i` →
`Alt+G I`, `?` → `Alt+?`, `Shift+G` → `Alt+Shift+G`. Only the first chord
changes, because only the first press can fire by accident; the rest of a
sequence is read only while it waits. Throws `BindingParseError` on a bad
string, like `parseBinding`.

exports.name: DEFAULT_REMAP_MODIFIER
exports.description: The modifier `withModifier` adds by default when remapping a character binding (K130): Alt works on every platform and the matcher's code fallback keeps it working on the macOS Option layer.

exports.name: reservedKeys
exports.description: The reserved keys of `platform`, canonical and resolved, for set lookups.

exports.name: analyzeKeymap
exports.description:
Analyzes the effective rules (highest priority first, as `Keymap.effective()`
returns them). Each pair is reported once.

exports.name: Finding
exports.description: One analysis result. `rules` are the rules involved, the winner first where there is one.

exports.name: RESERVED_KEYS
exports.description:
Keys a web page cannot have, per platform (K36): the browser or the OS acts
on them before (or instead of) delivering them to the page, in a normal tab.
Written with `Mod` where the key is the platform's primary modifier.

exports.name: AnalyzeOptions
exports.description: Options for `analyzeKeymap`: the platform to resolve keys for and which extra checks to run.

exports.name: createKeyboard
exports.description: Creates a keyboard engine. `M` is the command manifest type (`typeof manifest`).

exports.name: KeybindingFor
exports.description: A keybinding rule typed against a manifest: the command id is checked and `args` takes that command's arg type (K43, K140, K142).

exports.name: KeyboardOptions
exports.description: Options for `createKeyboard`: the platform, sequence timeout, conflict policy and start-up switches.

exports.name: DispatchEnv
exports.description: What the dom layer knows about the event that the core cannot see.

exports.name: DispatchDecision
exports.description: What one key event did (K35, K44).

exports.name: PendingSequence
exports.description: A sequence waiting for its next key (K22; the pending-chord indicator reads it, K116).

exports.name: ExplainEntry
exports.description: One rule's verdict for a stroke (K35).

exports.name: Explanation
exports.description: Why a key did or did not fire, rule by rule, highest priority first (K35).

exports.name: KeyboardPlugin
exports.description:
A plugin bundles commands, default keys, context providers and middleware
under a namespace (K119, K121, K125, K127). Every command id must start with
`name.`; `weight` orders its keybindings among other plugins'.

exports.name: KeymapConflictError
exports.description: Thrown by `bind` under the `error` policy (K34).

exports.name: Keyboard
exports.description: The engine, typed by its command manifest `M` (K140).

exports.name: keyboardMap
exports.description: Every command with each of its effective bindings, sorted by category, then title, then key (K147).
exports.signature: (keyboard: Keyboard, options?: { readonly includeUnbound?: boolean; }) => KeyboardMapEntry[]

exports.name: keyboardMapJson
exports.description: The map as pretty JSON with the platform it was resolved for.
exports.signature: (keyboard: Keyboard, options?: { readonly includeUnbound?: boolean; }) => string

exports.name: keyboardMapMarkdown
exports.description: The map as markdown: one `##` section per category, a table of command, keys, when and source (K147).
exports.signature: (keyboard: Keyboard, options?: { readonly title?: string; readonly includeUnbound?: boolean; }) => string

exports.name: KeyboardMapEntry
exports.description: One binding of one command (or a command with no binding: `key` null).

exports.name: MAP_FUNCTION_WHEN
exports.description: How a `when` written as a function reads in the map (it cannot be serialised).

exports.name: MAP_NO_CATEGORY
exports.description: The category of commands that declare none.

exports.name: keyBinder
exports.description:
A binder over `keyboard`. Each `bind` registers the command and its key
until disposed. The rule fires whatever overlay is on top (`ANY_OVERLAY`),
because the component's own surface (the open palette) is usually that
overlay and the same key must close it; its keys pass the smart input
policy, so Mod+K works from the palette's search field.

exports.name: KeyBinder
exports.description: The shape a key-owning component calls (structurally the overlay kit's `PaletteKeyBinder`).

exports.name: KeyBinderOptions
exports.description: Options for `keyBinder`: the command id, category and layer of the key it binds.

exports.name: PALETTE_TOGGLE_COMMAND
exports.description: The default command id: the palette's open / close key.

exports.name: hasDom
exports.description: True when a DOM exists (a browser or jsdom), false on a server or in a worker.

exports.name: isElementNode
exports.description: True for an element node from any realm (the parent page or a same-origin iframe).

exports.name: composedParent
exports.description: The parent of `node` across shadow boundaries: its slot, its parent element, else its shadow host.

exports.name: composedAncestors
exports.description: `node` and its composed ancestors, innermost first.

exports.name: eventElements
exports.description:
Elements on an event's composed path, innermost first (K94): a key typed in
an input inside an open shadow root reports the input, not the host.

exports.name: deepActiveElement
exports.description: The focused element, descending into open shadow roots (`document.activeElement` stops at the host).

exports.name: isEditableElement
exports.description:
Whether typing into `el` produces text (K88, K90): a text-like `input`, a
`textarea`, a `select` (letters pick options), an element with
`role="textbox"` (custom editors), or `contenteditable` other than `false`.
Inherited `contenteditable` is the caller's walk (`isEditablePath`).

exports.name: isEditablePath
exports.description:
Whether the innermost element of `elements` (a composed path, innermost
first) is a typing target (K88, K90, K94). Walks up for an inherited
`contenteditable`: the nearest element that sets the attribute decides, so a
`contenteditable="false"` island inside a rich-text editor counts as not
editable.

exports.name: attributeTokens
exports.description: Space-separated tokens of `attr` on every element of `elements`, innermost first.

exports.name: detectPlatform
exports.description: The platform the page runs on, from `navigator.platform` (feature data, not a UA sniff); `win` when unknown. For hosts building their keyboard.

exports.name: SCOPE_ATTR
exports.description: Marks a subtree as a named scope: while focus is inside it, the context key `scope.<name>` is true (K27, K131). Space-separated names allowed.

exports.name: REGION_ATTR
exports.description: Marks a landmark region; the innermost one around focus is the `focusedRegion` context key (K31).

exports.name: OWNS_ATTR
exports.description:
Keys a widget owns (K92): space-separated chords (`ArrowUp ArrowDown Home End j k`),
or `*` for every key. While focus is inside the element, the global
dispatcher leaves those keys to the widget's own handler.

exports.name: STICKY_ATTR
exports.description: Marks a sticky header the focus reveal must scroll past (K80); `thead` counts without it.

exports.name: SCOPE_PREFIX
exports.description: The prefix of scope context keys (`scope.editor`).

exports.name: strokeFromEvent
exports.description:
The stroke for `event`. `composing` is the dom layer's own composition flag
(between `compositionstart` and `compositionend`): some browsers report
`isComposing: false` on the key that ends a composition, so the flag is
OR-ed in (K9). AltGr comes from `getModifierState("AltGraph")` (K7).
